where: Section 1 and Section 2 prose, and Section 3 pulse paragraph
problem: The exponential is typed as plain text in several places ("A e−t/τ", "vC = Vs(1 − e−t/τ)", "i = (Vs/R)e−t/τ"), so a student reads "e minus t over tau" instead of e raised to −t/τ. Formulas elsewhere in the chapter use the superscript tag, so the notation is inconsistent.
fix: Use <sup> in every case: "A e<sup>−t/τ</sup>", "v<sub>C</sub> = V<sub>s</sub>(1 − e<sup>−t/τ</sup>)", "i = (V<sub>s</sub>/R)e<sup>−t/τ</sup>".

problem: "the output looks like a distorted copy of the pulse" does not say which quantity is the output. When Tp is much smaller than τ the capacitor voltage barely moves; it is the resistor voltage that copies the pulse shape, and the capacitor voltage is a small, rounded version of it.
fix: Say it explicitly: "if Tp is much smaller than τ the capacitor voltage barely moves and stays near its starting value; the resistor voltage (which equals the source minus the capacitor voltage) then looks like a distorted copy of the pulse."

problem: "SPICE transient analysis solves exactly this exponential update" is not accurate. SPICE steps time with numerical integration rules (backward Euler, trapezoidal, Gear) using a companion model; the exponential comes out as an approximation whose accuracy depends on the time step.
fix: Write: "SPICE transient analysis steps time with a numerical integration rule (trapezoidal or backward Euler) applied to the capacitor and inductor companion models, and shrinks the time step near switching; the result approximates the same exponential curve."

problem: "every voltage and current settles along the same exponential curve" can be read as saying all variables share one waveform. They share only the time constant τ; each has its own starting value, final value and sign, so some rise and some fall.
fix: "every voltage and current settles along an exponential with the same time constant τ; each has its own starting value, final value and sign."
